issues.claim: A handy format is an architecture decision record (ADR): context, the decision, consequences, the options considered.
issues.problem: The Nygard post (the only ADR source cited) defines Title, Context, Decision, Status and Consequences. It has no "options considered" section. The sentence presents the alternatives as part of that format. Alternatives appear in other ADR templates such as MADR.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: "ADR: title, context, decision, status, consequences; list the rejected alternatives in the context or add a separate section". Make the same change in the RU text.

issues.problem: The page is a corporate principles page. The fetched excerpt does support the "Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit" claim, so the link is fine, but the kind is imprecise.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep `article`, or use `docs` (the guide has no better kind).

issues.claim: And how would you know in advance that it is time to revisit it?
issues.problem: The second sentence of the hint points straight at one of the answer's steps (the revisit signal), so the hint is stronger than a nudge. The same applies to the RU hint.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten the hint to the first sentence: "How is 'I disagree' different from 'I keep the decision from working'?" Shorten the RU hint the same way.

issues.problem: The mechanical evidence reports the link as dead (TLS failure) and no excerpt was fetched, so it cannot be confirmed as a working source for the GDPR claim. A link that fails check-links will fail the weekly CI job.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace it with a URL that fetches successfully, for example https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679, or another official GDPR text. Re-fetch it and confirm it returns the regulation text. Update linkTitles if needed.

issues.claim: The ACM Code of Ethics explicitly requires avoiding harm (principle 1.2) and respecting privacy (principle 1.6), including collecting personal data only with the users' knowledge and consent and only as much as is needed.
issues.problem: The ACM page was not fetched (403), so no excerpt supports this claim. From memory, 1.2 (Avoid harm) and 1.6 (Respect privacy) are the right numbers. 1.6 clearly says to collect only the minimum personal information necessary. Its wording on consent concerns using data for other purposes and being transparent. "Only with the users' knowledge and consent" may overstate the text.
issues.suggestedFix: Re-fetch the ACM page (or cite a mirror such as https://www.acm.org/code-of-ethics/the-code-of-ethics-in-plain-text) and confirm the 1.6 wording. If consent is not stated, rephrase to: "respecting privacy (1.6), including collecting only the minimum personal information necessary and not using it for other purposes without consent". Make the same change in the RU text.

issues.problem: This is a general claim about store policies with no cited source. It is plausible, since app stores require disclosure of data collection and permission-based access to contacts and location, but it is not backed by a link.
issues.suggestedFix: Either keep it as an illustrative risk or soften it to "possible removal from app stores for violating their data-collection rules". Make the same change in the RU text.

issues.claim: Кто в компании владеет этим решением и какие риски видите вы, но, возможно, не видят они?
issues.problem: The hint points at two main elements of the answer, the decision owner and the risk, which is close to giving the answer away.
issues.suggestedFix: Weaken it to: "Кто в компании отвечает за такие решения и что им нужно знать, чтобы решить осознанно?" (EN: "Who is accountable for decisions like this, and what do they need to know to decide knowingly?").

issues.problem: The ACM Code is a professional standard rather than an article. `article` is acceptable but imprecise.
